nodes.summary: Staff and others who operate AI for the organisation get training suited to their role and to the people affected, and the training is recorded.
nodes.title: AI literacy programme

nodes.summary: A documented, approved AI policy says who may build, buy and approve AI, and is reviewed regularly.
nodes.title: AI policy

nodes.summary: Every AI system is recorded with an owner, and automated discovery looks for systems that are not recorded.
nodes.title: AI system inventory

nodes.summary: Roles for AI development, use, risk approval and oversight are named and kept separate where they should be.
nodes.title: AI roles and accountability

nodes.summary: Laws and standards that apply to AI use are recorded with an owner and reviewed when they change.
nodes.title: Register of AI obligations

nodes.summary: Anyone can raise a concern about an AI system through a known route, and concerns are tracked to a close.
nodes.title: AI concern reporting route

nodes.summary: Each system has a risk assessment that identifies, analyses, rates and treats risks to people and the organisation, including likelihood and size of impact, and is kept current.
nodes.title: AI risk assessment

nodes.summary: Before release, the effect of the system on individuals and groups is assessed and recorded.
nodes.title: Impact assessment on people

nodes.summary: Design choices, data origin, preparation, assumptions, suitability and known gaps are recorded for the data behind each model.
nodes.title: Training and test data governance

nodes.summary: Where each data set came from, and the original purpose of collecting any personal data in it, is recorded.
nodes.title: Data provenance record

nodes.summary: Data and outputs are examined for bias against people or groups, results are recorded, and bias found is detected, prevented or reduced.
nodes.title: Bias testing

nodes.summary: Each system has technical documentation, written before release and kept up to date, covering what the applicable rules require.
nodes.title: Technical documentation

nodes.summary: Users and deployers receive instructions covering purpose, limits, accuracy and how to use the output properly.
nodes.title: Instructions for use

nodes.summary: A system is tested against its requirements before release and after significant change, and the results are kept.
nodes.title: Pre-release verification and validation

nodes.summary: The system records events automatically across its lifetime, with enough detail to trace its behaviour and to spot risks.
nodes.title: Automatic event logging

nodes.summary: A running system is monitored for errors, drift and misuse, and alerts reach a named person.
nodes.title: Operational monitoring

nodes.summary: Named people with the competence, training, authority and support for the job oversee each system, understand its limits, can interpret its output and watch for over-reliance.
nodes.title: Assigned human oversight

nodes.summary: A person can disregard or override an output and can stop or deactivate the system, and who may do so is assigned.
nodes.title: Override and stop

nodes.summary: Workers and their representatives are told before an AI system is used on them at work, and that notice is recorded.
nodes.title: Informing workers

nodes.summary: People dealing directly with a system are told it is an AI, and a check confirms the notice is shown.
nodes.title: AI interaction disclosure

nodes.summary: Generated audio, image, video or text is marked as artificial in a machine-readable way, using a method that is effective, interoperable and robust as far as feasible, and a check confirms the marking.
nodes.title: Synthetic content marking

nodes.summary: A data processing agreement is in place before an AI supplier receives personal data.
nodes.title: Supplier data processing agreement

nodes.summary: AI suppliers are reviewed before use and regularly afterwards, including rights issues such as intellectual property, and the risk controls applied are recorded.
nodes.title: AI supplier risk review

nodes.summary: A written agreement sets out the information, capabilities, technical access and help a supplier gives so that the organisation can meet its obligations.
nodes.title: Supplier information agreement

nodes.summary: Before personal data goes to a supplier outside the EU, the transfer is checked and its legal basis recorded.
nodes.title: Cross-border transfer check

nodes.summary: Workloads hold only the AI permissions they use, and unused grants are found automatically.
nodes.title: Least-privilege AI permissions

nodes.summary: A system may send data only to approved AI endpoints, and a check confirms it.
nodes.title: Approved egress endpoints

nodes.summary: Cloud accounts running AI workloads meet a security baseline, and a check confirms it.
nodes.title: Cloud security baseline

nodes.summary: Personal data used by AI systems has a lawful basis, is kept to what is needed, and is protected.
nodes.title: Personal data safeguards

Data practices cover design choices, data origin and collection, preparation, assumptions, suitability of the data, and gaps in it.
Examine data sets for biases likely to harm people or lead to prohibited discrimination, and take measures to detect, prevent and reduce them.
Technical documentation is drawn up before a high-risk system is released, kept up to date, and shows that the system meets the requirements.
High-risk systems technically allow events to be recorded automatically over their lifetime, to support traceability and monitoring.
High-risk systems are transparent enough for deployers to interpret and properly use their output, and come with instructions for use.
High-risk systems can be effectively overseen by people, who can understand the system, avoid over-reliance on it, disregard or override its output, and stop it.
A high-risk provider and a third party supplying components or models agree in writing the information, access and help the provider needs to comply.
Duties of deployers of high-risk AI systems.
Deployers assign human oversight to people with the competence, training and authority it needs, and give them support.
Employers tell workers and their representatives before using a high-risk AI system at the workplace that they will be subject to it.

Providers design systems that interact directly with people so those people are told they are dealing with an AI, unless that is obvious.
Providers of systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text mark the output in a machine-readable way as artificially generated.
High-risk AI systems have a documented risk management system that runs as a continuous process across the whole lifecycle.
Identify and analyse the known and reasonably foreseeable risks the system can pose to health, safety or fundamental rights when used as intended.
